question: GQ-006
finding: people.sqlite (0.03 GB) holds 124,185 scored authors that were NOT migrated to v2. Unique, unbacked, and dismissed twice for being small.

author_value.columns: owner, score, tier, s_volume, s_peak, s_breadth, s_adoption, s_density, s_freshness, s_license, repo_count, cat_count, top_repo, total_stars, dependents_max, latest_push
author_value.reading: The v2 graph carries author_value inside person_content.meta_json for exactly 8 owners. The v1 table has 124,185. The scoring was effectively not migrated, so this is the only copy.

also_proven_redundant.reading: A filtered view of the live graph, not unique data. Fourth snapshot proven contained.

lesson: I ranked people.sqlite last twice — once for having no citations, once for being 0.03 GB. Both proxies failed. books.sqlite was uncited and turned out to be the catalogue; people.sqlite is tiny and holds the only copy of 124,185 author scores. Size and citation count are not evidence about content.
